brief: A three-quarter studio view of a carved copal-wood alebrije jaguar on a rough workbench, shot like a museum catalogue. Layered watercolour builds opaque-looking fields of turquoise, magenta, saffron and black. Over them, fine pen dots, chevrons and tiny eye-motifs are painted by a visibly human hand, slightly uneven. Hyperreal attention goes to the flaws: hairline cracks along the grain, a chipped ear showing pale raw wood, and wood shavings and a dropped brush on the bench. A warm, low workshop lamp rakes from the left and throws long soft shadows. The piece feels craft-honest and tactile, celebrating the object rather than the animal.

An overhead tabletop of halved pomegranates and golden quinces arranged into large circular medallions, with leaves and stems trailing like vines between them. The fruit is in dense, burnished coloured pencil: madder crimson arils with glassy highlights, quince skins in ochre and saffron with their faint fuzz, and leaf greens in deep olive. The ground is an unbleached cream linen cloth. Its weave is rendered with fine directional pencil, and a few juice stains bloom in rose watercolour. The composition is symmetrical and ceremonial, like a dowry cloth seen from above, but every seed is real and wet.

A tight portrait of a jazz trumpeter mid-blast, with cheeks ballooned and eyes squeezed shut. Every pore, vein and bead of sweat is rendered with photographic exactness, but the colour is arbitrary. Vermilion shadows sit under the jaw, viridian planes run across the forehead, cobalt fills the temple hollows, and the highlights are cadmium yellow. Juicy, overlapping watercolour washes have crisp dried edges, and dense coloured pencil restates the fine detail over them. The brass bell flares into the foreground in hot orange and violet. The background is a flat, unmodulated emerald. The image is joyous, loud and physically strained.

A cracked smartphone lies face-up on a dark slate countertop, its lockscreen glowing softly with a blurred beach photo. From a single impact point near one corner, a dense branching fracture spreads across the glass. It is drawn in feathery hairline pen that forks and forks again into fractal capillaries. Each crack line catches a sliver of prismatic light in thin edges of cyan and amber. The phone's notifications sit beneath the fracture in faithful grey type. The whole branching pattern has the dendritic logic of an electrical burn. The mood is quiet disaster: the tiny violence of a dropped object, examined with forensic patience.

A cut-crystal whisky tumbler, viewed straight down from above, sits on a black velvet field. A single point light below projects its facets outward as concentric rings of tiny sharp light spots, perfectly symmetrical. The glass itself is drawn in fine silver pen and white marker, with knife-edge facets and a meniscus of amber whisky. The surrounding spots are soft sprayed halos with hard white cores. They fade in intensity toward the edges and are faintly tinged violet and cyan. The image feels scientific and hushed, with order emerging from refraction.

A pair of cracked leather work gloves, still holding the curl of the hands that wore them, drawn as if etched. Dense cross-hatching and stippled pen in sepia-black capture every split seam, oil stain and frayed cuff. A pale watercolour rectangle of celadon tissue sits slightly off-register behind them. It is crisp-edged and faintly wrinkled, like a thin paper laid into the plate, and the drawing crosses its border unbroken. A ghostly plate-mark bevel frames the whole on warm ivory. The mood is restrained and archival: a printmaker's homage to labour.

An overhead view of tightly packed rows of sliced maki rolls on a black lacquer tray, each cross-section a concentric jewel. The rings run seaweed black, glistening rice white, salmon coral, avocado chartreuse and tamago yellow. Saturated wet-into-wet watercolour pools inside crisp pen boundaries, so each slice reads like a polished glass cane. Rice grains catch tiny white highlights, and the cut faces glisten. A smear of soy and a single wasabi dab break the grid. The composition is rhythmic and repeating, almost a bead pattern, yet unmistakably edible and freshly cut.

A grid of sequential cross-sections through a single pineapple, read left to right like a scan series on a black lightbox. Each slice is built in compressed charcoal and soft white chalk-like marks on near-black ground, with no colour at all. The fibrous core, the spiral eyes of the rind and the translucent wet flesh show in luminous greys. A thin dotted calibration line and tiny tick marks run along the margins. The edges of each section glow faintly as if backlit. The mood is cold, diagnostic and quietly beautiful. Absolute anatomical accuracy is delivered with the eerie flatness of a medical image.

Translucent ribbons of prosciutto are draped across a parchment-toned board. Their fat-rimmed edges meander like detailed coastlines, full of inlets and peninsulas. The meat is rendered in glassy watercolour layers of rose, garnet and pearly white fat, with a waxy sheen. Faded vermilion and verdigris rhumb lines radiate straight across everything from two pen-drawn compass roses. Tiny cartographer's lettering in brown ink names each "cape" along the fat edge. Foxing spots and a fold crease age the ground. The work is witty, scholarly and appetising, a navigator's map made of charcuterie.

A frontal hyperreal portrait of a market goat with a brass bell and a marigold garland, centred on a cream cotton-textured ground. Every whisker, eye-slit and hair tuft is defined by confident hand-drawn black pen outlines. Inside them sit muted natural-dye watercolour washes: indigo shadows, madder red garland, myrobalan yellow highlights and iron-black hooves. The colours soak slightly beyond the lines in soft bleeds. Fine parallel pen fills mimic the cloth's weave and the hair direction. A slender floral border frames the beast. The mood is earthy, warm and devotional, a temple-cloth sensibility applied to a very real animal.

The back of a young man's head and neck in tight close-up, just after a barber has sculpted a skin fade and a squared-off box top. The haircut is treated as clipped hedge architecture: crisp planes and sharp edges. Thousands of tiny graphite and blue-black coloured-pencil ticks build every hair, shortening to stippled shadow at the fade and to bare umber-brown skin with a razor-lined edge. A few loose clippings cling to the neck. The background is a flat warm barbershop mint. The tone is meticulous, geometric and affectionate.

Three magpie tail feathers fanned on a wet slate step. Their apparent black resolves into shifting nacre-like iridescence of bottle green, peacock teal, violet and bronze, rippling across each vane like the inside of a shell. Translucent watercolour glazes carry the colour, laid in layer over layer so the hues shift barbule by barbule. Hairline pen defines the rachis and the split vane edges. The slate is rough grey-blue charcoal mass beaded with water. The composition is diagonal and asymmetric, cropped hard at one feather tip.

A crumpled brown-paper grocery bag tipped on its side, three oranges rolling out. It is rendered in letterpress sensibility: two dense inks, vermilion and a heavy carbon black, on thick cream cotton stock. Forms are built from solid ink masses with squash halos at the edges. A slight misregistration lets the vermilion ghost past the black, and blind debossed creases suggest the bag's wrinkles. Hyperreal detail comes through tonal hatching set like engraved halftone: pore dimples on the peel and fibre tears in the paper. The bag sits off-centre, low and right, with generous uninked margin.

A lone motorcyclist approaches head-on across a blinding salt flat. Below the horizon, the air turns to liquid: a cobalt mirage pool reflects the rider upside down and smears their legs into wavering ribbons. Horizontal watercolour bands carry the image, with Naples yellow ground, scorched sienna shimmer and pale cerulean sky. The bands are deliberately broken and offset as if refracted. The rider's chrome headlamp, visor and boots stay coloured-pencil sharp at the core and fray into heat ripples at the edges. Most of the frame is empty, glaring and trembling.

A man's broad shoulder and upper back in a bathhouse, skin glistening, half-veiled by rising steam. Across it runs a traditional bodysuit tattoo of a carp climbing a waterfall amid wind bars and peonies. The tattoo is rendered as real pigment under real skin: bold black pen outlines softened by healing, and graded bokashi shading in indigo, vermilion and jade watercolour sinking into pores and stretching over muscle. Sweat beads carry pin-sharp highlights. The steam blurs into soft grey washes at the frame's edges, and the composition is cropped tight and monumental.

A paper cup of black coffee on a fold-down train table, its surface shivering with concentric ripples. The entire image is built only from long, horizontal, jittering black ink lines, like a drum-recorder trace. Tone comes purely from line density and amplitude. The lines are calm and widely spaced over the pale buff tabletop and tremble tightly in the cup's dark liquid. They spike violently where a ripple catches window glare. A single thin red-ink baseline runs straight across the lower third. The overall feel is clinical, vibrating and quietly tense.

A white dinghy sail fills the frame from below, swollen with a gust, its luff fluttering and its battens pressing through the cloth. Every surface is drawn as continuous flow-field streamlines in fine coloured pencil. The lines bend around the curvature exactly as air would, packed tight where the fabric tensions and loosening into the slack leech. Colour grades along each line from ultramarine at the windward edge through lilac into warm coral at the trailing edge. The sky behind is a sparser field of the same streamlines. The image reads like a meteorological chart that has become cloth.

A crowd of latex party balloons pressed against a ceiling, seen from directly beneath, so their round bellies hang like pouched storm clouds. Charcoal mass builds the deep slate shadows between the lobes. Each underside glows with soft watercolour in bruised mauve, copper, sickly olive and dusky rose, as if lit by late-storm light leaking from one side. Trailing ribbons curl down in sharp pencil. Static-clung hairs and tiny knot puckers add the hyperreal detail. The composition is all-over and claustrophobic, with no floor visible.

A full-face motorcycle helmet floats in three-quarter view against deep slate. Its right half is fully hyperreal: candy-apple red lacquer, a mirrored smoke visor reflecting a garage door, and scuffed decals. Toward the left, the surface dissolves progressively into a cyan fine-pen polygon mesh of triangulated quads and isolines tracing curvature. The mesh densifies where the shell bends sharply. The rendered half is built from soft airbrushed spray gradients with razor-edged specular glints. Pen lines stay hairline-thin and luminous. The seam between the rendered and wireframe halves stays ragged, like a render mid-calculation.

A close, frame-filling view of a dusty tractor tyre. Its chunky rubber lugs form an interrupted, off-kilter labyrinth of chevrons and stepped diamonds that echoes Kuba raffia patterning, where the pattern breaks and restarts without warning. The palette is limited to raw sienna dust, ochre, bone and soot-black rubber. Dense graphite and charcoal-like hatching gives the rubber a velvety, cut-pile nap, and crosshatched shadows sink deep into the grooves. Pale dust settles in drifts along every ridge. There is no sky and no context, only the tread as a woven-looking field cropped hard at all four edges.
